chunks: And what is in this book of the narration of Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) concerning the meaning of Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, saying "So he began striking [their] legs and necks" has been transmitted by me from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah Al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Imran Al-Nakha'i, from his uncle Al-Husayn ibn Yazid Al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, from Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both).

key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Al-Sadiq (The Truthful), title of Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for the interpretation of 'striking legs and necks' in Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides this specific isnad to authenticate the interpretation of the controversial verse in Surah Sad (38:26) regarding Prophet Sulayman's judicial act of 'striking legs and necks.' By tracing the chain back to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, the text underscores the Shi'a reliance on the Ahl al-Bayt for clarifying ambiguous Quranic narratives and historical events.
